description: The figure presents two side-by-side bar charts illustrating the relationship between inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss Kappa, and two distinct measures of sample-level ambiguity: Ambiguity Std (standard deviation of ambiguity scores across annotators) on the left, and Max Ambiguity (maximum ambiguity score assigned to a sample) on the right. In both charts, the vertical axis represents Fleiss Kappa, ranging from 0.0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, with values labeled above each bar. The left chart displays four bars corresponding to Ambiguity Std values of 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, with Fleiss Kappa values of 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24 respectively; the bars are colored in progressively lighter shades of blue as ambiguity increases. The right chart shows three bars for Max Ambiguity levels 1, 2, and 3, with corresponding Fleiss Kappa values of 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23, also shaded in descending intensity of blue. Both charts visually demonstrate a general inverse relationship: as ambiguity increases (either by standard deviation or maximum value), inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss Kappa) tends to decrease, with the exception of the third bar in the left chart (Ambiguity Std = 0.82, Kappa = 0.03), which shows a notably lower agreement than the subsequent level (Ambiguity Std = 0.94, Kappa = 0.24).
